Anna (runtime): FYI escalated ticket from Acme — they see p95/p99 regressions since last runtime deploy (around ~10:15 UTC). latency looks awful for short prompts :grimacing:
Mike (support): cc @Anna (runtime) can you paste the traces we gave them? they included a curl and a couple of timestamps. customer is frustrated, says 3x p95 on small payloads.
Anna (runtime): putting logs here. Observed metrics: p50 ~90ms (same), p95 jumped 120ms -> 360ms, p99 from 250ms -> 1.1s for text-gen short seq (<=64). Happens on model: open-llama-7b-quant, inference node pool gpu-a100-1.
Dalia (ml-kernel): thanks — earliest suspect is the recent kernel/attention change we merged last week (flashattn2 enabled by default + new compile flag FAST_KERNELS=1). also changed SDPA fallback threshold to 512 tokens.
Jason (infra): confirm deploy bot shows release 2026.03.11:a with compile flags: -O3 -march=native FAST_KERNELS=1. deploy-bot: release 2026.03.11:a applied to pool gpu-a100-1 at 10:12 UTC.
Kyla (oncall): I pulled a few traces from the p95 hosts, here's a snippet (logs sanitized):
```
[2026-03-11T10:20:14Z] KERNEL_SELECT: using flash_attn_v2 (fused_attention_kernel)
[2026-03-11T10:20:14Z] ATTENTION_IMPL: seq_len=32, beam=1, kv_cache_hits=0
[2026-03-11T10:20:14Z] LATENCY: total=370ms, kernel_attn=280ms, kv_copy=20ms
```
Anna (runtime): that kernel_attn number is the problem. flash_attn path is slower for many short sequences on this model due to attention layout mismatch (we saw this in perf bench but missed the fallout in prod).
Dalia (ml-kernel): repro steps I used locally:
```
# minimal repro curl
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-llama-7b-quant","input":"Say hi","max_new_tokens":32}' -w '\nTIME:%{time_total}s\n'
```
local before-change p95 ~0.09s, after-change p95 ~0.35s. Also tried forcing SDPA by setting env var REDWOOD_ATTENTION_PREF=sdpa and latency drops back to ~0.11s.
Mike (support): can we give customer a toggle they can set on their dedicated pool? they want a workaround now.
Jason (infra): quick mitigation: set model profile override to prefer sdpa for open-llama-7b-quant on affected pool. we can push config change to control plane, no need for binary rollback. I can roll to 100% within 10m.
Anna (runtime): plan: 1) immediate mitigation: enqueue config override to prefer sdpa for the affected model/pool (Jason), 2) short-term: revert FAST_KERNELS compile flag and rebuild image for the pool (Dalia + infra), 3) longer-term: add per-model perf heuristics to choose between flashattn/sdpa automatically (product/eng follow-up).
Dalia (ml-kernel): patch idea: change SDPA fallback threshold back to 128 and add microbench during model load to pick best kernel by sampling ~50 warmup runs. I'll open PR with tests.
Kyla (oncall): I'm going to start canary: apply sdpa-prefer override to 5% of nodes -> watch p95/p99, then 25/100. alerting rule already fires on 2x baseline p95.
Anna (runtime): customer message template (Mike, feel free to send):
"Hi — we observed a regression after a recent performance-oriented build. We've applied a targeted configuration change to prefer the SDPA attention kernel on your reserved pool which should restore prior latency within minutes. We're also rebuilding the runtime without the FAST_KERNELS compile flag and will follow up once the fix is deployed. Apologies for the disruption and thanks for patience. — Anna + Runtime team"
Mike (support): sending now. I'll include repro curl we gave them and ask them to confirm after we flip override. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: rollout started: model-profile override 'prefer:sdpa' -> pool gpu-a100-1 (5% nodes)
Kyla (oncall): monitor: p95 on canary nodes dropped from ~360ms -> ~110ms within 3 mins. p99 also dropping.
Jason (infra): starting staged config rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 30 min if metrics good. I also queued an infra rebuild with FAST_KERNELS=0, build id 2026.03.11:b.
Dalia (ml-kernel): filing follow-up ticket: add model-level kernel-choosing microbench + unit tests that run in CI; make FAST_KERNELS opt-in per-model not global.
Anna (runtime): postmortem notes to add: missed perf test case for short sequences, lack of model-level kernel sampling. assign to runtime + ml-kernel.
Mike (support): customer confirmed latency back to normal after our change. closing urgent escalation. I'll leave a note on the ticket to expect a rebuild and full fix next week.
Anna (runtime): thanks all. action items: Dalia PR + tests, Jason complete rebuild and coordinate canary binary when ready, Kyla keep alert watch for 24h.
Jason (infra): ack. I'm adding a temporary dashboard tile showing kernel selection counts (flashattn vs sdpa) and per-kernel p95.
Dalia (ml-kernel): quick note for triage: avoid using -march=native in release builds; it can produce code paths that diverge across hosts and expose perf cliffs.
Kyla (oncall): closing thread when rebuild live and 24h stable. :white_check_mark:
